determination.primary: The timeout is most consistent with the 90s Payload travel deadline expiring while the explicit PvE role/loadout flow was still pending; it is not the Toolbox 180s window itself
determination.not_just_180: Start to Deploy was 215.844s, but Toolbox 180s is only initial launch stability and had already returned once client/server were healthy; the Payload 90s timer begins at open and is independent
determination.pawn_predicate: The predicate itself is strict (same-world GameState/NetDriver, PB pawn, acknowledged/possessed, Alive). The server file has no per-line event timestamps; its 08:36:15 heartbeat marker precedes the role/spawn block, so this is an ordering marker rather than an exact spawn time. The run does not prove the predicate was wrong at the 90s deadline: the server spawn block occurs only after the long role/loadout interaction. After timeout, server eventually spawned and the client rendered/accepted control, demonstrating late recovery at game/network level but not Payload state recovery
determination.recovery: No Payload status recovery was observed or implied: timeout clears proof/scope and leaves connectStage Failed; game continued due underlying game/server lifecycle. Do not report client native Playable from the late screenshot alone
determination.risk: If testers spend more than 90s between direct open and native pawn readiness, the UI/game can become playable while strict Payload status is Failed, creating false-negative readiness and possibly clearing online proof state. This offline run does not establish an online admission impact, but the shared client state machine is a distribution risk for online launches too

recommended_next: Before any release claim, run a separately authorized fast-path or source fix review: either make the offline role/loadout phase pause/extend the offline deadline, or prove an online-safe deadline policy tied to actual native admission milestones. No change was made in this review.
